sentence: The company is looking for a ___ candidate to lead the marketing department.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun 'candidate'; 'qualified' means having the right skills.

sentence: Ms. Tanaka was ___ promoted to regional director after the merger.
explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'was promoted'.

sentence: The new software has greatly improved the ___ of our payroll process.
explanation: After 'the', a noun is needed, and the singular noun fits 'improved the ___ of'.

sentence: All applicants must ___ a résumé and two reference letters.
explanation: After 'must', the base form of the verb is needed.

sentence: Mr. Lopez is an ___ manager who always meets his deadlines.
explanation: An adjective is needed to describe the noun 'manager'.

sentence: The ___ of the new training program will begin next Tuesday.
explanation: After 'the', a noun is needed, and 'of the new training program' follows it.

sentence: Our customer service team responds to complaints ___.
explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'responds'.

sentence: Staff members are ___ to attend the safety briefing on Friday.
explanation: 'Are required to' is a passive structure followed by an infinitive.

sentence: The committee will make a ___ decision about the budget next week.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun 'decision'.

sentence: Interns are expected to work ___ with the senior engineers.
explanation: An adverb is needed after the verb 'work'.

sentence: The ___ period for the sales position closes at the end of the month.
explanation: 'The application period/process' idea: 'application' (a noun for a process) fits; an 'applicant' is a person and cannot close.

sentence: Mr. Evans was praised for his ___ to the project.
explanation: After the possessive 'his', a noun is needed.

sentence: The firm offers ___ salaries to attract skilled engineers.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the plural noun 'salaries'.

sentence: We are pleased to announce that the factory will ___ production next month.
explanation: After 'will', the base form of the verb is needed.

sentence: Ms. Cho gave a very ___ presentation to the board of directors.
explanation: An adjective is needed after 'very' and before 'presentation'; 'convincing' describes the presentation.

sentence: Employees who are ___ with the new schedule can speak to their supervisor.
explanation: After 'are', a participial adjective describing people is needed: 'dissatisfied'.

sentence: The manager asked for a detailed ___ of the quarterly expenses.
explanation: After the adjective 'detailed', a noun is needed.

sentence: Please read the instructions ___ before you assemble the cabinet.
explanation: An adverb is needed after the verb phrase 'read the instructions'.

sentence: The company's ___ growth has attracted many new investors.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun 'growth'.

sentence: Mr. Kim is ___ for approving all travel requests.
explanation: After 'is', an adjective is needed: 'responsible for'.

sentence: The ___ of the old computer system took three weeks.
explanation: After 'the', a noun is needed; 'replacement of' names the action.

sentence: The seminar will be ___ useful to new managers.
explanation: An adverb is needed before the adjective 'useful'.

sentence: Ms. Dubois is widely ___ as an expert in international trade law.
explanation: 'Is regarded as' is a passive construction that needs a past participle.

sentence: Our ___ goal this year is to reduce shipping costs.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun 'goal'; 'primary' means main.

sentence: The training session was ___ attended by staff from every branch.
explanation: 'Well attended' uses the adverb 'well' with a past participle.

sentence: To ensure ___, all visitors must sign in at the front desk.
explanation: After 'ensure', a noun is needed as the object: 'security'.

sentence: The supplier delivered the order ___ than expected.
explanation: A comparative form is needed because of 'than expected'.

sentence: Mr. Rossi's ___ in the field made him the obvious choice for the job.
explanation: After the possessive 'Mr. Rossi's', a noun is needed, and 'experience' is uncountable here.

sentence: Ms. Garcia is considered the most ___ designer on our team.
explanation: An adjective is needed after 'the most' to describe the noun 'designer'.

sentence: The two companies reached an ___ after months of negotiation.
explanation: After the article 'an', a noun is needed.

sentence: Delays in shipping were ___ caused by bad weather.
explanation: An adverb is needed between 'were' and the past participle 'caused'.

sentence: The workshop offers a ___ introduction to project management.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun 'introduction'.

sentence: Because of the ___ in demand, the factory hired fifty more workers.
explanation: After 'the', a noun is needed; 'the increase in demand' is the standard phrase.

sentence: The store manager was ___ to learn that sales had doubled.
explanation: A participial adjective describing a person's feeling is needed: 'delighted'.

sentence: Please notify us ___ if your address changes.
explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'notify'.

sentence: The ___ of the building will be completed by the end of June.
explanation: After 'the', a noun is needed, and 'of the building' follows it.

sentence: Our company values ___ communication between departments.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun 'communication'.

sentence: Applicants should have a ___ understanding of financial reporting.
explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun 'understanding'.

sentence: The new policy applies ___ to all full-time employees.
explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'applies'.
